subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Derivative Control: Predicting the Future
description: A short lesson to help you apply Derivative Control: Predicting the Future.

hook.text: If the error is shrinking fast, ease off early. The derivative term predicts where the error is heading.

buildup.text: The derivative term responds to the rate of change of the error, not the error itself.

discovery.text: It acts as a brake — damping oscillations and reducing overshoot before they happen.

twist.text: Noisy signals make the derivative spike wildly. A low-pass filter on the derivative term tames this.

climax.text: Robotic arms, drone stabilizers, and precision positioning stages rely on derivative action.

punchline.text: React to the trend, not the gap — derivative anticipates and dampens.

quiz.question: Why is derivative control sensitive to noise?
options: Noise causes rapid changes in the error signal, which the derivative amplifies
Derivative control only works with analog signals
